# Test fixtures

All fixtures are synthetic. Never add real thread dumps here: they contain host
names, URLs, client IPs and sometimes user data.

| Fixture | Reproduces |
|---------|------------|
| `aem-node1-*.dump` | JDK 11 series: stuck request, monitor and `ReentrantLock` contention, CPU growth |
| `jdk21-deadlock.tdump` | JDK 21 header format (`#31 [4101]`, decimal `nid`), deadlock report after `JNI global refs` |
| `jdk8-app.log` | JDK 8 dump inside an application log, CRLF line endings |
| `aemcs/` | AEM as a Cloud Service, generated by `make_aemcs_fixtures.py` |

`aemcs/` is an anonymized model of a real production data set (136 dumps, 17 JVMs)
that tdscope was validated against. It keeps the shapes that mattered there: client-IP
request thread names, the Jetty acceptor, background `socketRead0` threads, unusual
lock lines, Oak `CacheLIRS$Segment` contention and a JVM restart inside one pod. The
tests in `tests/test_aemcs.py` pin down the results verified on the real data, and
`tests/test_consistency.py` checks every fixture with the same method used on the
real dumps: parsed threads, frames, states and lock lines must equal naive line counts
of the raw text.

After changing the generator, regenerate the files (a test fails if they are stale):

```bash
python tests/fixtures/make_aemcs_fixtures.py
```
